generation_members.surface_form: A curated dataset of 476 binary ionic compound melting temperatures spanning 0-4,000°C was compiled for machine learning model development.
The best one-step gradient-boosted tree regression model achieves 165±4 K MAE and 0.89 R² on the test set for melting temperature prediction.
Models trained without elastic moduli features yield errors greater than 400 K, demonstrating that elastic features are necessary for accurate melting temperature predictions.

Tree ensemble methods (gradient-boosted trees and random forest regression) substantially outperform linear models, which achieve MAE >240 K and RMSE >340 K, at least 100 K worse than non-linear approaches.
